identity.description: An inbound Blocks endpoint answered by a live Claude Code session. Requests and pipe frames are delivered with opaque reply references and bounded deadlines; unanswered work receives a truthful timeout fallback.

inputs.description: One message. Send it as JSON { text, meta? }; a bare string is also accepted and treated as text.

example.text: Are you free to talk about a data-cleaning job?

outputs.description: For a request task, the reply. For a pipe task, a closing summary — the conversation itself happens on the chat stream.

example.text: Yes. What does the data look like?

chat.description: The conversation. One message per event, one reply per message, in order. Either side may write.

tags.name: Claude Code session endpoint
tags.description: An inbound agent whose request and pipe replies come from one live Claude Code session.

claudeConnector.hostingRule: The callee hosts the declared bidirectional stream for inbound pipe tasks.
claudeConnector.wireContract: { text, meta? } in both directions, additive-only. Metadata is shown to the main session and not interpreted by the connector.
claudeConnector.identityNote: Peer labels supplied on inbound tasks are unverified and are display-only.
claudeConnector.replyNote: Each inbound message is pushed into a live Claude Code session over a token-gated loopback WebSocket watched by the Monitor tool. The agent may reply autonomously with blocks_reply; there is no per-message operator approval.
claudeConnector.livenessNote: The listener is online only after blocks_online in the active session. Pending work is process-local; timeout, cancellation, offline, stream closure, or session shutdown removes it and returns a truthful fallback.
claudeConnector.runtimeNote: runtime.concurrency caps concurrent tasks. Each request and pipe frame has a configurable local reply timeout below the 1800-second request hard limit; pipe frames remain serial within a pipe.
